reasoning: Both attempts cut each block to one instance, set properties before parenting, spread work across frames with a budget, and pass all checks. The deciding difference is criterion 4: B reserves every saved cell in `occupied` before queuing the load, so nobody can place into a cell that is still loading. A only claims cells as it creates blocks, which leaves a race in which saved blocks get skipped. A's write-up even treats this as intended. A has a somewhat more efficient unload (a cursor over its own table instead of a one-frame GetChildren walk) and uses template cloning, but B's correctness while a build is loading matters more.

criteria.note: Owner/PlacedAt values replaced by `part:SetAttribute("PlacedAt", placedAt)` and the per-plot `blocks` table; placed time kept for saved and new blocks.
`templates[blockType]:Clone()` gets its CFrame and attribute set, then `part.Parent = plot.folder` comes last.
The Heartbeat `runJobs` shares a 4 ms / 500-block budget across `stepLoad` and `stepUnload` (cursor-based) and destroys the empty folder at the end.

Cells are only marked in `occupied` as each block is created in `stepLoad`, so anyone in reach can place into a cell that is still loading and the saved block gets skipped. Leaving mid-load is handled well (`isClosed` plus the unload job frees cells).
Removal requires `plot.blocks[block]` in the player's own plot plus `getReachableRoot`. Placement validation is unchanged.
Says builds appear over about 0.7–3 s at the budget, has a 'Not yet verified' section, and lists what players will notice, though it accepts the loading-cell race as intended behavior.
Only Builds.server.luau and the doc change, the code is fully typed, and all checks pass.
`blockRecords[part] = {OwnerId, PlacedAt, Cell}` replaces the value objects, and PlacedAt is kept for saved and placed blocks.
`Instance.new("Part")` has all its properties set, then `part.Parent = parent`.
`onHeartbeat` shares 200 blocks per frame across the load and unload queue, but `onPlayerRemoving` still walks `GetChildren()` of up to 20k parts in a single frame.
`reserveCells` marks every saved cell before queuing. On leaving mid-load, reservations from `NextIndex` onward are released and the created parts go to `Doomed`.
Keeps `IsDescendantOf`, compares `record.OwnerId` with UserId, and keeps the reach check. Placement validation is unchanged, and records are cleared on leave so removal is rejected during unload.
States about 1.7 s per full build at 200/frame and about 13 s for 8 simultaneous joins, is explicit that nothing was measured, includes a verification plan, and lists what players will notice.
Scoped to Builds.server.luau and the doc, fully typed with a PlotState union, and all checks pass.

strengths: Template cloning with the attribute and parent set last
Resumable cursor unload that uses the cell keys it stored, with no GetChildren
Shared time and block budget across all jobs
Handles leaving mid-load and a full server waiting for a slot
weaknesses: Does not reserve a save's cells before yielding, so placements can race into cells that are still loading and saved blocks get skipped
Several waiting players all wake on slotFreed and race for the slot (harmless but untidy)

strengths: Reserves every cell before the first yield, so no races
Clean state machine (Loading/Ready/Unloading) with correct cleanup when a player leaves mid-load
An orderly waiting-player queue hands freed slots on
Thorough, honest write-up with a verification plan
weaknesses: Leaving walks GetChildren over up to 20k parts in one frame
Unload uses part.Position as the cell key instead of the stored Cell
No template cloning (property writes for every part)
